ONE MATERIAL DIRECTIVE

Generalize the binary rank-three elbow to the exact finite-alphabet frontier rank(A_b) = 2m−1 for every treatment alphabet size m ≥ 2.

Exact result and proof:

Let R = row(A_b) and S = span{r_z : z ∈ A_X} = {𝟙⊗t : t ∈ ℝ^m}. If every target row is in R, then S ⊆ R and dim S = m. Identify branch rows with matrices φβ ψβᵀ. Define F(M) = [M𝟙] ∈ ℝ^m / span{𝟙}. F vanishes on S. Since ψβ is a probability state, F(φβ ψβᵀ) = [φβ]. Treatment-effect completeness makes these images span the (m−1)-dimensional quotient. Hence the induced map R/S → ℝ^m/span{𝟙} is surjective, so rank(A_b) = dim R ≥ m + (m−1) = 2m−1. This also forces at least 2m−1 tagged treatment branches.

The bound is attained by one normalized 2m−1-branch instrument. Put ρ_i = ½e_i + (1/(2m))𝟙, i = 0,…,m−1. These strictly positive probability states form a basis: their column matrix is ½I + (1/(2m))J, with eigenvalues 1 and ½. Use treatment branches (½e_i, ρ_0), i = 0,…,m−1, and ((1/[2(m−1)])𝟙, ρ_j), j = 1,…,m−1. Their effects sum to 𝟙; their effect and state families both span ℝ^m. The first m rows span {a⊗ρ_0}; the remaining m−1 span {𝟙⊗q : q ∈ span(ρ_1,…,ρ_{m−1})}; these subspaces intersect trivially, giving rank exactly 2m−1. They contain 𝟙⊗ρ_i for every basis state ρ_i, hence contain every target row r_z. Pair this with the terminal basis instrument {(e_y,e_y)}. The existing bow row-span theorem then identifies every Q_{z,y}, while 2m−1 < m² proves non-tomography. For m=2 this construction is exactly the current three-branch menu, since ρ_0=(3/4,1/4) and ρ_1=(1/4,3/4).

Scoped changes: add the m-ary menu definition and exact 2m−1 lower-bound/attainment theorem; state the all-query m-ary GID corollary using the existing bow iff theorem; retain the binary results as the m=2 specialization/regression fixture; update TL;DR, project justification, interpretation, related work, and honest scope from binary rank three to the finite-alphabet 2m−1 frontier; leave the one-fixing causal-lift OEQ unchanged.

Their positivity assumption requires each vertex mechanism matrix to have strictly positive entries. Theorem 1 identifies the entire semantic causal structure only for Markovian DAG models, and the discussion explicitly says the paper solved only the Markovian case. Primary version of record: https://www.mdpi.com/1099-4300/27/7/732. Oxford version-of-record PDF: https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid%3A41b3380f-db42-492a-b032-172ed1738a0e/files/rm039k701g. Therefore the note’s named separable MIC condition is the Proposition 6 specialization, but its primitive-positive edge-source bow class is not Friend et al.’s published theorem class. The overall results are incomparable—not an inclusion transfer: the note restricts probes to separable branches and strengthens source-level structure/positivity, while allowing latent bow confounding and identifying queries rather than whole Markovian mechanisms.
